name: OnlyFans
tagline: Subscription platform where creators charge fans monthly for gated posts, DMs, and pay-per-view media.

pricing.basis: platform commission on creator earnings, subscription prices set by each creator
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Free to join, revenue share model rather than a flat monthly fee.

verdictSummary: The software here is a paywall in front of a media feed, which is genuinely a weekend project. Everything expensive is off to the side: high-risk payment processing that most processors refuse outright, age and identity verification for every creator and everyone appearing in a frame, chargeback and fraud handling, DMCA takedown machinery, and the audience that already has a card on file. You can self-host a gated content site in an afternoon and it will work perfectly right up until you need to charge a stranger money. Stripe, PayPal, and nearly every mainstream processor prohibit adult content, so the DIY version either stays safe-for-work or dies at checkout. Build it as a personal paid-content site and it is fine; build it to replace the platform and you have built a very nice front door with no bank behind it.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted site where paying members unlock gated posts and media, with tiers, a member feed, and Stripe subscriptions for safe-for-work content.
requirements: A Stripe account, which permits paid memberships but not adult content
Object storage or a VPS with disk for media, plus bandwidth budget for video
Your own audience, since there is no discovery
whatYouLose: Payment processing that will actually accept adult content, plus the chargeback and fraud operation behind it
Discovery and an existing base of fans with saved payment methods
Age and identity verification, record keeping, and the compliance paperwork that comes with it
Leak detection and DMCA enforcement, however imperfect
Mobile-grade video delivery: transcoding, adaptive streaming, global CDN
Built-in DMs, tips, and pay-per-view plumbing with dispute handling
moatNotes: Payments for this category are a licensing and risk problem, not an engineering one. The banking relationships are the product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Fans pay because the creators they want are there and checkout takes one tap on a card the platform already has. Creators stay because the alternative is negotiating with a high-risk payment processor, running their own age verification, eating chargebacks, transcoding video, and chasing leaks, all for a cut they might not actually beat after fees. The commission looks steep until you price out doing the unglamorous half yourself. Self-hosting works well for creators with an existing mailing list and safe-for-work content, and badly for everyone else.
notes: The paywall is a weekend; the payment rails are not. The moat is banking relationships for a category most processors ban, plus a few hundred million fans with a card already on file.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted paid membership content site. Single project, runs locally with one command.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Tailwind for styling, Stripe for subscriptions, local filesystem for media storage.

Scope, in:
- Single creator, many members. One admin account (me), read via ADMIN_EMAIL in .env.
- Posts: title, markdown body, optional image or video attachments, visibility of public or members-only or tier-gated.
- Tiers: name, monthly price, description. Stored in SQLite, mapped to Stripe Price IDs.
- Member signup: email magic link auth (log the link to the console in dev, send via Resend if RESEND_API_KEY is set).
- Stripe Checkout for subscribing, Stripe Billing Portal link for members to cancel or update cards, and a webhook route that syncs subscription status into SQLite.
- Member feed at /feed showing posts the member's active tier unlocks; locked posts render title plus a blurred teaser and an upgrade button.
- Media served through an authenticated route, never a public static path. Signed short-lived URLs, no direct file listing.
- Admin UI at /admin: create, edit, delete posts and tiers, upload media, list members and their tier and status.
- Seed script that creates two tiers and three sample posts.

Scope, out: DMs, tips, pay-per-view one-offs, comments, video transcoding, adaptive streaming, mobile apps, discovery or search, analytics, email campaigns, referral links.

Hard constraints:
- All secrets in .env: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, ADMIN_EMAIL, AUTH_SECRET, optional RESEND_API_KEY. Ship a .env.example, never commit real keys.
- No telemetry, no third-party analytics, no CDN dependency.
- Stripe prohibits adult content. Put a plain comment at the top of the Stripe module saying so, and do not pretend otherwise anywhere in the code or docs.
- Video files over 100MB should be rejected at upload with a clear message, since there is no transcoding pipeline.

Deliver a README with setup steps, how to create Stripe products, how to forward webhooks with the Stripe CLI, and one honest paragraph on what this does not handle: chargebacks, age verification, leak enforcement, and bandwidth cost.
